name: Pre-incident preparation
steps: Maintain pre-approved forensic imaging hardware (write blockers, verified blank media).
Document the organization's IR escalation chain and legal contact list (in-house counsel, outside counsel, law enforcement).
Define the authority chain: who may seize a device, with what internal authorization.
Pre-test the imaging workflow on similar hardware; keep checksums of the tooling itself.
Identify the jurisdiction(s) the evidence may be presented in and note admissibility requirements.
tools: Tableau write blockers, FTK Imager, hardware hashers
notes: Preparation failures invalidate chain of custody more often than acquisition errors.

name: Identify and scope potential evidence
steps: Identify systems of interest: affected hosts, servers, network gear, cloud accounts, removable media.
Prioritize by volatility: memory > running processes > network > disk (live acquisition order).
Record system names, roles, IP/MAC addresses, time zone and current UTC offset.
Interview the system owner re: passwords, encryption, and unusual activity observed.
Check for FDE (BitLocker/FileVault) — if recovery key unavailable, do NOT shut down (lose memory) without a plan.
tools: Asset inventory, IR runbook, encryption-status check (manage-bde / csrutil)
notes: Document every system touched — scope creep later looks like negligence.

name: Preserve original evidence
steps: Write-block the source media; never boot the original disk r/w.
Image with verified hashes (SHA-256) before and after acquisition; record hash values.
For live systems: capture memory first, then acquire logical files (hiberfil.sys, pagefile, unallocated where feasible).
Disable backup overwrites; snapshot cloud VM volumes before further access.
Keep the original evidence byte-for-byte untouched; work only on copies.
tools: FTK Imager, dd/ewfacquire, Guymager, cloud snapshot APIs
notes: The verified hash is the single most challenged item in court — record both source and copy hashes.

name: Collect volatile and persistent data
steps: Memory: dump with tool built for the OS (WinPmem, LiME, vmss2core) — document tool version + SHA256.
Collect process list, network connections, logged-on users, event logs (Security/System/PowerShell), registry hives.
Collect browser artifacts, shell artifacts (Recent, Prefetch, Jump Lists), scheduled tasks, services.
For cloud: collect API logs (CloudTrail/ActivityLogs), IAM role last-used, MFA events, without exposing secrets.
Label every artifact with source system, collector, date/time, and hash.
tools: WinPmem, LiME, KAPE, FTK Imager live, Carbon Black/XDR exports
notes: KAPE's '!SANS_Triage' module automates the standard triage collection set.

name: Forensic imaging
steps: Acquire physical disk image (RAW/DD or E01) via write-blocked hardware or verified software write-block.
Record drive model, serial, size, partition layout before imaging.
Compute SHA-256 on source and image; verify independently.
Store images on authenticated media; label with case number, exhibit number, date, initials.
Verify image integrity with the original hash before analysis begins.
notes: Use E01 for compression+hash metadata; retain the raw hash for court.

name: Analysis on copies only
steps: Work exclusively on a bit-identical copy or mounted image (read-only).
Document the analysis toolchain with versions (and tool hashes if required).
Record findings in a timeline with artifact, source evidence, and analyst.
Preserve 'raw' extracted artifacts (files, registry keys, event rows) as exhibits.
Hash every extracted artifact that becomes an exhibit (malware samples, scripts, config).
tools: Autopsy, EnCase, X-Ways, Volatility, Eric Zimmerman tools
notes: Analysis records = the audit trail that makes the report defensible.

name: Documentation of custody
steps: Create the chain-of-custody log: item, description, source, date/time, handler, transfer, reason.
Every transfer requires: two signatures (transferor/recipient), timestamp, purpose, and seal status.
Photograph the exhibit, its surroundings, and the original state of the system.
Record all passcodes/encryption keys received (in sealed, restricted-access storage).
Attach the acquisition hash sheet to the case file.
tools: CoC template, case management (e.g. Autopsy case, FTK case), camera
notes: Gaps in documentation create admissibility risk — document before, during, after.

name: Transport and storage
steps: Use tamper-evident bags and sealed containers for physical media.
Track storage location access via sign-in sheet or electronic access log.
Maintain environmental controls (temperature/humidity) for long-term storage.
Barcode or unique-ID every item; log physical moves in the custody ledger.
Secure the evidence room with restricted access + CCTV where policy requires.
tools: Tamper-evident bags, evidence lockers, asset tag system
notes: Digital evidence also needs logical access control: encrypt at rest, RBAC, audit trail.

name: Return or disposition
steps: Return original media only after case approval and verification of integrity (re-hash).
For disposal: degauss, shred, or cryptographically wipe per policy; document method + witness.
Retain the case record (images, notes, hashes) for the retention period required by policy/law.
Remove exhibits from the chain log with signatures confirming receipt back by owner/law.
Preserve a complete copy of the case file for potential legal challenge.
notes: Disposition must be documented as carefully as acquisition.

name: Cloud and virtualized evidence
steps: Snapshot the VM volume and memory (if available) via provider API; note snapshot IDs and times.
Capture IAM access logs, key rotations, login events (CloudTrail, Azure AD sign-ins, GCP audit).
Preserve the instance metadata: instance ID, AMI/image, launch time, attached IAM role.
Export from managed services with official export functions; record the export job ID and completion time.
Do not assume the provider's retention covers your needs — snapshot early.
tools: AWS CLI, az CLI, gcloud, provider console exports
notes: Cloud evidence often lives in immutable logs with fixed retention — collect before expiry.

name: Report with evidence mapping
steps: Produce the final report mapping each finding to the artifact name, path, and exhibit number.
Include the acquisition summary: tool, version, hash, and a copy of the CoC log.
Include the timeline of events and any artifacts that contradict or corroborate the timeline.
State limitations explicitly (encrypted volumes, logs unavailable, tool version constraints).
Have a second analyst (or supervisor) peer-review the report before release.
tools: Report templates, timeline tools, case file
notes: A finding without an exhibit reference is a rumor, not evidence.
